stem: What is a content calendar?
options: A schedule of what to publish, when and where
A list of the competitors' posts
A report of last month's followers from the start
A folder of unused photos
explanation: A schedule of what content will be published, when and on which channel.

stem: Which tool is commonly used to edit short videos for TikTok and Reels on a phone?
options: CapCut
Excel
Postman
AutoCAD
explanation: CapCut.

stem: Why use a social media scheduling tool such as Metricool or Buffer-like platforms?
options: To plan and publish across channels and track results
To buy followers for the accounts
To translate posts into most the languages in many setups
To remove the need for a content plan for the business
explanation: To plan and publish posts across channels at the best times and track performance in one place.

stem: A short video loses most viewers in the first three seconds. What should be improved?
options: The hook in the first seconds
The length of the end credits
The file name of the video
The size of the logo in the corner
explanation: The hook: the opening seconds must show value or curiosity immediately.

stem: Which metric best shows whether content builds an audience rather than just reaching people once?
options: Follower growth with repeat engagement and shares
Impressions in a single day within the team during the project
The number of posts published in day-to-day work for the project
The size of the image files in many setups in practice
explanation: Follower growth and repeat engagement or saves and shares, not reach alone.

stem: What is conversion rate?
options: The share of visitors who complete the desired action
The number of visitors in a month in most teams for the project
The cost of acquiring one visitor
The time visitors spend on the page in a real project at that stage
explanation: The share of visitors who complete a desired action.

stem: What is an A/B test?
options: Showing two versions to random halves of the audience
Testing the page on two different browsers in day-to-day work
Asking two managers to approve the page within the team
Running the page for two weeks in a row
explanation: Showing two versions to randomly split audiences to see which performs better.

stem: A test is stopped after one day because variant B is ahead. What is the problem?
options: Stopping early inflates the risk of a false result in the long run
One day is the standard length for each test
Variant B should usually be declared the winner at once
Tests should be run on weekends alone
explanation: Stopping early (peeking) inflates false positives; decide sample size and duration in advance.

stem: What does the ICE scoring framework rank experiment ideas by?
options: Impact, confidence and ease
Income, cost and effort
Interest, clicks and engagement
Idea, channel and execution
explanation: Impact, Confidence and Ease.

stem: Heatmaps show that visitors never scroll to the call-to-action button. What should you test?
options: Moving the call to action higher on the page for the project
Making the button grey so that it is less visible
Adding more text above the button
Removing the heatmap tool from the site altogether
explanation: Move the call to action above the fold or make the page shorter, then A/B test it.

stem: What is a welcome flow in marketing automation?
options: An automated email series triggered by a new subscription
A survey that is sent to each customer once during the project
A banner shown on the first visit
A discount given to employees
explanation: An automated series of emails triggered when someone subscribes.

stem: Which metric tells you what share of recipients opened an email?
options: Open rate
Bounce rate
Click-to-open rate
Unsubscribe rate
explanation: Open rate.

stem: Why segment an email list?
options: Relevant messages to groups raise engagement
It lowers the cost of the email server
It removes the need to write some subject lines
It guarantees that each email is opened
explanation: Relevant messages to specific groups raise engagement and reduce unsubscribes.

stem: What does a hard bounce mean?
options: The address is permanently invalid and should be removed
The inbox was full for a short time in most cases for the project
The recipient marked the email as important at that stage
The email was opened on a phone during the project for the project
explanation: The address is permanently invalid, so it should be removed from the list.

stem: Which practice most improves email deliverability?
options: Authenticate the domain with SPF, DKIM and DMARC
Send more emails per day to the whole list
Use many images and no text in the email
Write most of the subject lines in capital letters
explanation: Authenticate the domain (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) and keep a clean, engaged list.

stem: Which of these is an Indonesian e-commerce marketplace?
options: Tokopedia
Notion
Trello
Zoom
explanation: Tokopedia (and Shopee, Lazada, Bukalapak).

stem: Which element of a product listing most affects search ranking and click-through?
options: A clear keyword-rich title and a strong main image
The date the seller joined the platform during the project
The colour of the shop banner
The number of products in the shop
explanation: A keyword-rich, clear title with a strong main image.

stem: In marketplace ads, ROAS is calculated as...
options: Ad revenue divided by ad spend
Ad spend divided by ad revenue in many setups
Clicks divided by impressions in many setups
Profit minus the shipping cost as the work grows
explanation: Revenue from ads divided by ad spend.

stem: A product has high views but a low conversion rate. What should you check first?
options: Price, reviews, photos and description in many setups
The size of the warehouse
The name of the shop owner
The time the page loads in other countries
explanation: Price, reviews, photos and description: the listing quality and offer.

stem: A flash sale sells out in an hour and the seller cancels many orders. What is the main marketplace risk?
options: Poor seller metrics that lower ranking and account standing
Lower prices for each future product in most teams in practice
A ban on all advertising for a year
A requirement to open a physical store from the start for the business
explanation: Cancellations and late shipments hurt seller metrics, ranking and account standing.

stem: In Google Ads search campaigns, what does CPC mean?
options: Cost per click
Cost per conversion rate
Customers per campaign
Clicks per customer
explanation: Cost per click: what you pay each time someone clicks your ad.

stem: What is a negative keyword?
options: A word that stops ads showing for irrelevant searches
A keyword with a very low bid
A keyword that triggers the lowest position from the start
A keyword reported as spam by users in day-to-day work
explanation: A word that stops your ad from showing for irrelevant searches.

stem: Which factors make up Quality Score?
options: Expected CTR, ad relevance and landing page experience
Bid amount, daily budget and number of keywords
Impressions, reach and frequency
Device type, location and time of day
explanation: Expected click-through rate, ad relevance and landing page experience.

stem: CTR is 5% and a campaign gets 2,000 clicks. How many impressions did it get?
explanation: Impressions = clicks / CTR = 2000 / 0.05 = 40,000.

stem: A campaign spends its whole daily budget by noon and misses afternoon buyers. What is the best first step?
options: Adjust budget, bids and ad schedule to spread the spend
Add more broad keywords to find buyers for the business during the project
Pause the campaign for a whole week in most teams for the project
Switch each ad to the display network within the team in the long run
explanation: Adjust the budget, bids and ad schedule or targeting so spend is spread across the high-converting hours.

stem: What does SEO aim to increase?
options: Organic traffic from search engines in most cases as the work grows
Paid clicks coming from advertisements on other sites
Followers on social media
Subscribers to an email list
explanation: Organic (unpaid) traffic from search engines.

stem: Which free Google tool shows the queries that bring users to your site and its indexing problems?
options: Google Search Console
Google Ads Editor
Google Forms
Google Drive
explanation: Google Search Console.

stem: Which is an on-page SEO factor?
options: A title tag that matches the search intent
The number of followers on the brand's Instagram account
The advertising budget of the month
The colour of the logo
explanation: Title tags, headings and content that match the search intent.

stem: What is a backlink?
options: A link from another site to yours
A link from your page to your homepage
A saved copy of your page for the business
A redirect from the http to the https version
explanation: A link from another website to yours; quality links are a ranking signal.

stem: Two pages target the same keyword and compete in the results. What is this called and what is a typical fix?
options: Cannibalisation, fixed by merging or differentiating the pages
Duplicate ads, fixed by raising the bid
Link rot, fixed by deleting old links
Crawl budget, fixed by adding more images
explanation: Keyword cannibalisation; merge the pages or differentiate their intent and use canonical tags.

stem: Which tool is used to create and manage Facebook and Instagram ads?
options: Meta Ads Manager
Google Search Console
Canva Presentations
Shopee Seller Centre
explanation: Meta Ads Manager.

stem: What is the Meta Pixel used for?
options: Tracking actions on your website to measure ads
Resizing images for the feed in many setups in a real project
Scheduling posts in advance in most teams in day-to-day work
Moderating comments on the page in day-to-day work
explanation: Tracking visitor actions on your website to measure and optimise ads.

stem: What is a lookalike audience?
options: People similar to your existing customers
People who already bought twice
People who follow your competitors from the start
People who live in your city
explanation: People who resemble your existing customers, built from a seed audience.

stem: Which campaign objective fits a goal of selling products from a catalogue?
options: Sales
Awareness
Traffic
Engagement
explanation: Sales (conversions / catalogue sales).

stem: An ad's click-through rate falls while frequency rises over weeks. What is the likely cause and fix?
options: Ad fatigue, fixed by new creatives and a wider audience
A broken pixel, fixed by reinstalling the app
A low budget, fixed by pausing most the ads
A wrong time zone, fixed by changing the account currency
explanation: Ad fatigue; refresh creatives and widen or rotate the audience.

stem: In GA4, what is the basic unit of measurement?
options: Events
Pageviews alone
Sessions alone
Hits
explanation: Events.

stem: What do UTM parameters do?
options: Tag links so traffic is attributed to a campaign
Speed up the loading of linked pages
Encrypt the links that are shared
Shorten the links for social media
explanation: They tag links so analytics can attribute traffic to a source, medium and campaign.

stem: What is Google Tag Manager used for?
options: Managing tracking tags without editing code each time
Designing the layout of landing pages
Buying advertising space on partner sites for the project
Storing customer data in a database
explanation: Managing tracking tags on a site without editing code each time.

stem: A funnel shows 10,000 visitors, 3,000 add to cart, 1,500 start checkout and 1,200 buy. Which step has the biggest relative drop?
options: Visit to add-to-cart, with a 70% loss
Cart to checkout, with a 50% loss
Checkout to purchase, with a 20% loss of buyers
There is no drop at some step
explanation: Visit to add-to-cart loses 70%; cart to checkout loses 50%; checkout to purchase loses 20%.

stem: Last-click attribution gives all the credit to the final touchpoint. What is a weakness?
options: It undervalues the earlier touchpoints that started the journey
It counts each purchase twice in reports
It cannot be used with paid campaigns
It needs a signed contract with the platform
explanation: It undervalues earlier touchpoints such as awareness campaigns that started the journey.
